findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:19: `queued = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import, causing every subsequent assignment source in the process to share the same timestamp instead of its instance creation time; use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

goldens.comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:19: `queued = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import, causing every subsequent assignment source in the process to share the same timestamp instead of its instance creation time; use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same issue: the timezone.now() default value in the AssignmentSource dataclass is evaluated once at class/module definition time rather than at instance creation time, causing all instances to share the same timestamp. The candidate even provides the same solution (using field(default_factory=timezone.now)) that would fix this classic Python mutable default argument anti-pattern.
